blocks.text: The journal of a punk photographer from Wollongong to London and back – in pictures

Katelyn Slyer’s book, The Middle, records a generation of young people negotiating their identity while caught between the intimacy of the analog era and new digital world from 2004 to 2010. Her photographs explore the ideas of becoming and connection in Australian and English punk scenes

Katelyn Slyer feeds ‘Boris’ the possum (who had been misgendered) with her baby in the kitchen. Boris would sneak into her bedroom and eat the Iced Vovos stashed under the bed. Photograph: Katelyn Slyer
Katelyn Slyer
Mon 23 Nov 2026 09.00 ESTLast modified on Mon 23 Nov 2026 15.43 EST

My friend Jemima arriving at our home in Austinmer on the New South Wales south coast after pulling an all-nighter from Sydney. The house was nicknamed The Love Shack – a half-condemned house with million-dollar views that overlooked the rock pools between the water and the escarpment. A lot of the photos from The Middle were taken during the time we lived there. Lorikeets used to perch on our Hills Hoist, flying over to our hands, which we would cover in honey

After living in London for a while I ran out of money and was couch-surfing/squatting with friends. I knew Katie from Wollongong. We moved in similar circles back home, but we became close while I was living in England. When I had nowhere to stay, she let me stay at her place, even when her housemates were reluctant. We got up to all sorts of mischief. This portrait is of Katie and Alberto, an Italian punk who I met in Camden
Landscape of the Port Kembla stack in 2005. It dominated the Wollongong skyline for nearly half a century before it came down in 2014. I always appreciate a gritty industrial landscape

In the early 2000s, whenever the Melbourne crew would visit, we would take them on adventures to local spots around Wollongong. We loved hanging out in the old tunnels under Hill 60, a second world war underground military fort. It was a bit creepy and fun to explore, and had rad views. This image is Dan and Sikk Mikk admiring Five Islands off the coast of Port Kembla

Christopher Zero mucking around in London with souvenirs after hours, when the tourists had gone home and the markets were being closed down for the night. I like this image as it encapsulates a snapshot of the time, showcasing royal memorabilia of that era

Before Austinmer, I used to live in Coniston, a suburb of Wollongong. During that time, I met Shane and Emma, who lived up the road from me. They always had wild and memorable parties with all the local skate crew, punks, hippies and everybody in between. They also had a massive skate ramp in their back yard

Az and Lulu were a well-known couple growing up in the Wollongong punk scene. Here they lie in MacCabe Park next to the youth centre one late afternoon. People grow and change but these images remind me of my past and make me nostalgic for moments that would otherwise be forgotten with the erosion of time and brain rot

Patto, from the Footscray crew, did himself some mischief and ended up on crutches. I appreciate his attention to detail, styling the crutches to suit his aesthetic. And the fact that it matched the couch at the pub perfectly. When I took the photo it was a happy snap. What I appreciate most about it now is the smaller details of his surroundings. The textures and the decor

An impromptu portrait of Rachelle in Sydney. I transitioned from a point-and-shoot film camera and started experimenting with my first digital camera. Rach is one of my beautiful mates who has allowed me to practise and hone my artistic skills and techniques. Any time we hung out she would be up for anything I threw her way

Hannah, my favourite Welsh gal. This image was taken at a gig in Soho at the 12 Bar, one of the local haunts that always had great bands playing. Hannah didn’t take herself too seriously and would always crack me up with her wit and intellect. I liked loitering out the front shooting the goings on between there and the Intrepid Fox

Once our friends started to have kids, we would find wholesome activities to do so we could keep hanging out. The Punk Cricket team was created and we would play at Conno school on the weekends. This is a portrait of my mate Lowki getting amped for the game. Lowki has a great voice, charisma and awesome stage presence. He was lead vocalist in Wollongong punk band Run 4 Cover and 3KD

When the Wollongong crew would visit the Melbourne crew, we would stay in Footscray and get up to all types of shenanigans. This boozy shot of Dan was taken on the way back from the annual Melbourne Punx pub crawl that happens to fall on AFL grand final day

Little Barry Jr and Bruiser. Baz was always a character with many cool stories and yarns to tell of a life well lived. When I came back from London, I lived with him for a while when the girls moved out. Eventually, I too moved and he became the custodian of The Love Shack until it was sold and demolished

When I was a teenager my family moved from Sydney to Wollongong. It was a big change for me at 16, leaving my friends and starting in a new town. One of the first friends I made was Erin. She was a couple of years older, super creative, made her own clothes, and had good taste in music. She was also my first friend who got pregnant and became a mother. This image is of her at the Austinmer rock pools with her two daughters, Zoe and Ella. Looking back, we were so lucky to have this spot to grow up and have fun in our back yard. The Middle was a formative time in my life. Not only was I growing and exploring individual identity, I was able to grow with them and witness their childhood close up
Back in 2009, I took a trip with my partner, Stevie, around Europe. Tucked away in a fjord near Molde in Norway was his mate Pauli’s back yard skate ramp
This was taken in Wombarra, in northern Wollongong, at a friend’s house at night. Dogs and goats hanging out together. I don’t remember their names, or much of this evening

DeeDee and Jemima. This image epitomises Aussie barbecue vibes. We had an old red Weber my folks had given me. We would cook up a barbecue and have jelly-wrestling parties in a blow-up pool in our yard
